contract: F-13's write-once config/kit-support.txt, the month a Kit's support period ends (plan W-17, G-13 (b), W-20, Appendix B F-13; docs/app-updates.md §8.4, §5.9 table B.10 'Support end'). Release 1 and every later version read this file on every Kit for ever; only the Kit builder writes it, once
provenance: Hand-written on 2026-11-26 at commit c168648c (T3.3b), before kit-support.ts and write-kit-support.mjs existed (tests first), from W-17, G-13 (b), F-13 and W-33 (plan §2, Appendix B), the record's §8.4 and §5.9, the P3 entry decisions 11 and 12, the T3.3b blast-radius sheet (its findings F2 and F3, the parameter table of its §4, the reader proposal of its §5, the rows S1-S8 and G1-G3 of its §8) and the orchestrator's answers to the sheet's questions (Q1 a node helper with one TS format module; Q2 the parameter required in a dry run; Q3 no upper bound, the value echoed in words; Q4 the read tolerance frozen here with its writer; Q8 the same month kept, another refused, unsold stock re-stamped by deleting the file on purpose), with ISO 8601's calendar month (YYYY-MM) as the outside source. No expected value was taken from the reader's or the helper's output. T3.3a's PROVENANCE.md in this folder is not edited: this file carries its own provenance, and the golden manifest (../../golden-fixtures.sha256) locks it
frozen: `read` is F-13's frozen half: what release 1's reader (readKitSupport) makes of every file a drive may hold at config/kit-support.txt, for ever; no answer there ever changes, and a new case is a new vector. P6's T6.4a computes the support notices from the month it returns and adds no parse of its own. `builder`, `writes` and `values` pin the HEAD builder's helper (scripts/lib/write-kit-support.mjs), which is replaceable: a later builder may word its lines differently, but every file it writes must be one `read` returns as a month

readers.readKitSupport: readKitSupport(rootPath) (src/main/services/updates/kit-support.ts): absent | unreadable (code: the errno token, never a message) | damaged (fault: not-a-file, empty, too-large, not-a-month) | month (month: the YYYY-MM string). Sync, never throws, no cache, logs nothing. Shown in the Copy report as `Support end: <YYYY-MM>`, `absent` or `unreadable` (damaged shows as unreadable, record §5.9)
readers.helper: node scripts/lib/write-kit-support.mjs --target <drive root> --support-end <YYYY-MM> [--check]: exit 0 written or kept (with --check: nothing written, the month echoed in words), 1 refused or failed (nothing written, an existing file untouched), 2 usage, or a support end that is no month or is before this computer's current UTC month

parts: as vectors.json: a vector's bytes are its parts joined, `text` as UTF-8, `base64` decoded, `repeat` repeated `times` times. A byte-order mark and bytes that are not UTF-8 are held as base64, and every character outside ASCII is a JSON escape: such bytes in a text file under tests/ fail the repo hygiene nets
at: where the vector's bytes go, under a scratch drive root: `file` (the default when `parts` is given) config/kit-support.txt holds the parts; `absent` (the default without parts) config/ exists, no stamp; `no-config` no config folder; `config-is-file` config is a regular file; `config-link` config itself is a link (a junction on Windows) to a folder that holds the parts as kit-support.txt; `folder` a folder at the stamp's name; `file-link` a symbolic link to a file holding the parts (Windows: only with the symlink privilege); `dangling-link` a symbolic link to nothing (the same); `folder-link` a link to a folder (a junction on Windows); `fifo` a named pipe (macOS and Linux only); `deny-read` the file holds the parts and its reader is refused reading it. In `writes` also: `no-target` the target folder does not exist; `target-is-file` the target is a regular file

read.name: reading the stamp is denied
read.why: there, but the read failed just now: the errno token only (F-11's content-free rule); shown as `unreadable` (record §5.9)

builder.why: W-17, the sheet §5 and brief decision 3: what the Kit builder writes for a month: the 7 ASCII bytes of the month and one LF (0x0A), 8 bytes, no byte-order mark, created exclusively (never through or over a link or an existing file)

writes.why: each vector puts `at` (as in `read`; parts or none) under a scratch root and runs the helper with --target <root> --support-end `supportEnd` (and --check when `check`). `stamp`: `builder` (config/kit-support.txt holds `builder.text` for that month, exactly), `untouched` (the bytes put there are still there, and a regular file's modification time too; for a link or a folder, still that link or folder), `none` (nothing at the stamp's name; with `no-target` the target was not made either). `stdout`: the one line printed. `stderr`: words the one refusal line holds (each of the helper's lines starts with `kit-support.txt:`)

vectors.why: W-17: written by the Kit builder

values.why: the --support-end value, each run with --check on a fresh drive: exit 0 with the month echoed in words (`stdout`), or exit 2 with `stderr` among the helper's line. The sheet §4: exactly 7 ASCII bytes, YYYY-MM with a month 01-12, matched whole, never trimmed; not before this computer's current UTC month (a fixed past value here; the boundary rows build their values from the test's own clock); no upper bound (Q3). A value that is no month is not echoed: it is free text
